title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the 'suite' of La Longue Marche, around ms. p. 672. It continues the structure theory of a group scheme Z~_{ρ,σ} over a base S_0 (written Z~_{g,σ} on the previous page). That group scheme maps to Aut_gr(𝔖^+) × G_m × μ × μ (the invariants μ, ε_2, ε_3, or ν', ν_2, ν_3). It is filtered as Z~ ⊃ Z~^{+0} ⊃ Z~^{+00} ⊃ ...; (55)–(56) on the previous page describe Z~^{+0} as an extension involving ₄G_a.

The innermost piece. Z~^{+∞} consists of the elements whose invariants ν', ν_2, ν_3 all vanish. Equation (57) identifies it with pure 'translation data': pairs (α_0, β_0) in M × M satisfying the compatibility (1-ρ_M)α_0 = (1-σ_M)β_0. Here M = Zλ_0 ⊕ Zλ_1 carries two automorphisms.

The actions, read off from (60):
- ρ: λ_0 ↦ λ_1, λ_1 ↦ -λ_0 - λ_1. This has order 3.
- σ: λ_0 ↔ λ_1. This has order 2.
- Together they generate the S_3 (Weyl group) action on the A_2 root lattice.

This suggests that Z~_{ρ,σ} is an automorphism or centralizer group scheme of affine (semidirect) data M ⋊ ⟨ρ,σ⟩ attached to the order-3 and order-2 generators of a free product Z/3 * Z/2 ≅ PSL_2(Z) (modular / Teichmüller-tower context). The pair (α_0, β_0) then gives the translation parts of the lifts of ρ and σ, and (57) is a cocycle-type compatibility.

Grothendieck's argument, step by step:
1. He claims Z^{+∞} is smooth of relative dimension 2 in characteristic ≠ 3.
2. He claims it is canonically a vector group (a 'schéma en Modules'): (58) Z^{+∞} ≃ V(P).
3. P is the rank-2 free Z-module defined as the kernel of M × M → M, (α_0, β_0) ↦ (1-ρ)α_0 - (1-σ)β_0, as in (59).
4. In coordinates α_0 = a_0λ_0 + a_1λ_1 and β_0 = b_0λ_0 + b_1λ_1, the map is (61): c_0 = a_0 + a_1 - b_0 + b_1 and c_1 = -a_0 + 2a_1 + b_0 - b_1.
5. One checks that c_0 + c_1 = 3a_1. So the image is the index-3 sublattice {c_0 + c_1 ≡ 0 mod 3}, as in (62).

Characteristic 3. Mod 3 one has c_1 = -c_0, so the 2×4 matrix has rank 1. The fibre of the kernel group scheme over F_3 therefore has dimension 3, not 2. This is the margin remark: 'en car. 3 ce n'est plus vrai'.

Where it leads. The 'Remarques' begin to treat points defined over Ẑ coming from M[0]. On the next page this becomes the congruence μ ≡ 1 - 2ν_3 (mod 3). There the image condition 2ν' - ν_2 + ν_3 ≡ 0 (3) is shown to be automatic for such points. This leads to the refined definition (63) of Z~_{ρ,σ}, with an auxiliary integer ν'' and the equation (1-ρ)α_0 - (1-σ)β_0 = 3ν''λ_1.

The mod-3 index computed on this page is exactly the source of that 3ν''λ_1 term.
errors: The map M×M → M in (59)/(61) is not surjective over Z: its image is the index-3 sublattice c_0 + c_1 ≡ 0 (mod 3). So the exact sequence (59) ending in '→ M → 0' is wrong as written. Grothendieck's phrase 'C'est un homom. surjectif' is half-retracted on the page, and the image is then described correctly in (62).

Because the cokernel is Z/3, the kernel group scheme is not a vector bundle over all of Spec Z or S_0. Its F_3-fibre has dimension 3. So (58) Z^{+∞} ≃ V(P) holds only over Z[1/3]. The margin note acknowledges this ('en car. 3 ce n'est plus vrai').
Minor: the main text says 'lisse en car ≠ 3', consistent with the above, but (58) is stated without that restriction.

ideas.what: Identifying the deepest filtration step of an automorphism/centralizer group scheme with a vector group V(P), where P is the kernel of (1-ρ, -(1-σ)): M×M → M for the S_3 action on the A_2 lattice.
ideas.modern_name: Kernel of a morphism of vector group schemes; group-scheme version of 1-cocycles / translation parts of affine lifts of Z/3 * Z/2 actions
ideas.where_published: Not as such; the context is the unpublished sequel to La Longue Marche (1981)

ideas.what: Observation that smoothness and the vector-bundle structure fail exactly at the prime 3, because the image has index 3 (c_0 + c_1 = 3a_1). This explains a 3ν''λ_1 correction term in the later definition (63).
ideas.modern_name: Bad prime / non-flat cokernel phenomenon for group schemes of automorphisms of Z/2 * Z/3-type structures

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up integral (over Z or Ẑ) group schemes Z~_{ρ,σ} with a multi-step filtration and explicit mod-2 and mod-3 invariants (μ, ν', ν'', ν_2, ν_3). These appear to describe automorphisms of modular / Teichmüller-type structures attached to the order-2 and order-3 generators. The characteristic-3 degeneration is noted but not worked out on this page. It is a small technical thread inside a larger unpublished construction, not an independent result.
missed.quote: en car. 3 ce n'est plus vrai
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only marginally: it records Grothendieck's attention to integral, bad-prime behaviour of the group schemes in his Teichmüller/Galois program. No new theorem is evident on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine linear algebra (a kernel and an image lattice of index 3) inside a larger unpublished construction. It is correct apart from the self-corrected surjectivity claim, and contains no standalone new idea.
transcription_corrections: The page header is probably the manuscript page number '672' (the first digit is written like σ), not 'σ 72'.
In (57) and elsewhere the subscript is ρ (as transcribed), while the previous page's 'g,σ' is the same symbol ρ.
(59): the arrow labels and maps are correct, but note that the handwritten 'M' at the left is overwritten as 'P' (0 → P → M×M → M → 0).
(61): c_0 = a_0 + a_1 + (b_1 - b_0) and c_1 = 2a_1 - a_0 - (b_1 - b_0), as transcribed. These are consistent with (60).
Margin note reads approximately 'en car. 3 ce n'est plus vrai — relation λ_0 ... λ_1 ... 3 !' (uncertain); 'x ^ z' in the transcription is doubtful.
